# Magic vs Wing Assistant: pricing and coverage compared (2026)


David Merriman


Co-founder, Magic


Updated Oct 2026


Table of Contents


11 min read


Published by Magic. Pricing and service information checked October 20, 2026 against the providers’ pages linked below. Confirm current terms with each provider.


## Quick Summary


Magic and Wing are both fully managed services. Each one recruits, trains, and replaces your assistant for you, and both publish their prices.


Both services price by tier. Magic’s Virtual Assistant plan is $360 a week for 40 hours ($9 an hour), while its Executive Assistant plan is $540 a week for 40 hours ($13.50 an hour) and includes Magic 24/7. The comparison below separates general and executive assistant plans and identifies the included hours and billing period.


What we found


- **Wing’s headline price is their entry tier, not their executive one.** The $999 plan is a general assistant. Executive-level support on Wing’s own price list is $1,999 a month.
- **Against that executive tier, Magic vs Wing comes down to about a dollar an hour.** Magic’s Executive Assistant plan is $13.50 an hour and Wing’s is $12.49, and Magic’s Executive Assistant price includes backup coverage.
- **Magic includes[Magic 24/7](https://getmagic.com/magic-247-assistant/) on full-time Executive Assistant plans.** Wing offers standard weekday coverage and custom extended schedules, including 24/7, by arrangement. Confirm backup scope in your quote.
- **Magic accepts the top 0.5% of applicants.** Providers use different selection measures, so published percentages are not directly comparable.

### Compare virtual assistant and executive assistant tiers separately


For day-to-day support, compare Magic’s Virtual Assistant plan at $9 an hour with Wing’s general assistant tier at about $6.24 an hour on its full-time plan. For executive work, compare Magic’s Executive Assistant plan at $13.50 an hour with Wing’s executive assistant tier at about $12.49 an hour. These rates use each provider’s stated included hours; weekly and monthly packages contain different numbers of hours.


Over a 52-week comparison, Magic’s standard EA plan provides 2,080 scheduled hours for $28,080. Twelve Wing EA monthly invoices provide 1,920 listed hours for $23,988. These calculations assume continuous service at unchanged rates and exclude additional fees. Compare the coverage and tasks included as well as the totals.


Magic’s Virtual Assistant plan is $1,440 per four-week billing cycle for 160 hours. Its Executive Assistant plan is $2,160 per four-week cycle for 160 hours. Wing lists $999 per calendar month for 160 general-assistant hours and $1,999 for 160 executive-assistant hours. Compare the same tier and annual hours as well as the invoice amount; a year contains 13 four-week cycles and 12 calendar months.

## Who covers the work when your assistant is away


Assistants take holidays, get sick, and go on leave. What happens to the work during those days is worth checking before you sign with either service.


Magic’s full-time Executive Assistant plan includes[Magic 24/7](https://getmagic.com/magic-247-assistant/) , a shared pool of assistants who pick up tasks when your dedicated assistant is unavailable. You send the request and someone handles it, at 2 a.m. or on a holiday.


Wing’s FAQ describes a standard contiguous eight-hour window, five days a week. Custom extended coverage, including 24/7, is available by arrangement. Ask which hours and absence-cover arrangements your quote includes.


Source:[Wing coverage FAQ](https://wingassistant.com/faq/) . Checked October 20, 2026.


## AI tools


Every Magic assistant gets access to leading LLMs and AI tools, plus[training](https://getmagic.com/feature/training/) on how to use them before they start working with you. Magic pays for the tools, and coaches each assistant one on one every week after that.


Wing describes its assistants as AI-trained. Their site doesn’t name the tools or describe the training, so you’d need to ask on the call.


## Vetting and training


Magic accepts the top 0.5% of applicants, and a person makes the final call after live interviews with each candidate. Wing also describes a vetting and training process. These claims use different candidate pools and measures, so they do not establish a relative acceptance rate.


Every Magic assistant goes through[training](https://getmagic.com/feature/training/) and assessments on AI tools before their first task for you. Wing says it handles matching, vetting, and training before an assistant touches your work, without detailing the curriculum.


## Contracts and cancellation


Magic has no long-term contract; its standard billing period is four weeks, with weekly billing also available. Wing advertises monthly plans. Wing says you can cancel anytime and doesn’t state whether a notice period applies. Magic lets you cancel at any time.
The other difference is when you commit. Wing starts with a 15-minute consultation, then matches you and goes live within 48 hours. With Magic you meet your assistant first, and there’s no charge until you start working together.


## Why choose Wing Assistant


If you need a niche specialist from a single managed service, look at Wing. Their site lists more than 155 role types across 27 industries, from bookkeepers to sales development reps, which is broader than what Magic covers.


Their general assistant tier at $999 a month full time is also the lowest published price in this comparison, and they advertise going live within 48 hours. If the work is routine and budget is the deciding factor, that tier is Wing’s strongest offer. Executive-level support on their own price list costs about double it.


## Why choose Magic


Choose based on the work you need covered, the included hours, and the backup service. Both Magic and Wing have separate general and executive assistant tiers.


Magic’s Executive Assistant plan includes Magic 24/7. For everyday work, Magic also offers a lower-priced Virtual Assistant plan.

## Magic vs Wing: common questions


Magic vs Wing: which is cheaper?


Wing has the lower hourly price in both full-time tiers shown here: about $6.24 for a general assistant versus $9 for Magic’s Virtual Assistant, and about $12.49 for an executive assistant versus $13.50 for Magic’s Executive Assistant. Magic provides 40 hours a week; Wing lists 160 hours per calendar month. Magic’s Executive Assistant plan includes[Magic 24/7](https://getmagic.com/magic-247-assistant/) . Compare the same tier, hours, and coverage when choosing.


How much does Magic cost?


Magic’s Virtual Assistant plan is $360 a week for 40 hours ($9 an hour). Its Executive Assistant plan is $540 a week for 40 hours ($13.50 an hour) and includes[Magic 24/7](https://getmagic.com/magic-247-assistant/) . Magic Teams is $540 a week per assistant, with custom hiring and training and discounts at scale. The prices shown use standard four-week billing. Weekly billing is also available through Sales at different rates. Part-time plans are available; contact Magic for current rates and hours. There is no charge until you start working with your assistant. See the[pricing page](https://getmagic.com/pricing/) .


How much does Wing cost?


Wing publishes two tiers on its site. A general virtual assistant is $699 a month part-time or $999 a month full-time. An executive assistant is $1,299 part-time or $1,999 full-time. Both plans are 80 or 160 hours a month. Other roles and locations have separate pricing; confirm the relevant plan and any fees.


Which Wing plan is the right comparison for Magic?


Compare Magic’s Virtual Assistant plan with Wing’s general assistant tier, and Magic’s Executive Assistant plan with Wing’s executive assistant tier. Magic’s EA plan includes Magic 24/7. Compare the work covered and total hours as well as the headline price.


Where are the assistants based?


Magic assistants are in the Philippines and Latin America, and all of them work US time zones. Wing’s site says its assistants are global or US-based without listing countries, and says pricing varies by role, experience, and location.


What happens when my assistant is on leave?


Magic’s full-time Executive Assistant plan includes[Magic 24/7](https://getmagic.com/magic-247-assistant/) , a shared pool of assistants who pick up tasks when your dedicated assistant is unavailable. Wing offers a standard eight-hour weekday schedule and custom extended coverage, including 24/7, by arrangement. Confirm the backup scope in your quote.


Do the assistants use AI tools?


Yes. Every Magic assistant gets access to leading LLMs and AI tools, plus[training](https://getmagic.com/feature/training/) on how to use them before they start. Magic pays for the tools. Wing describes its assistants as AI-trained, but doesn’t name the tools or describe the training on its site.


What happens if my assistant isn’t the right fit?


Magic replaces them at no extra cost and your saved preferences carry over, so the new assistant starts with the same context. On full-time Executive Assistant plans, Magic 24/7 handles urgent work while the new assistant is matched. Wing’s site commits to a free replacement within 24 hours.


Can I cancel anytime?


Magic has no long-term contract and you can cancel at any time. Wing also runs month to month and says you can cancel anytime, though its site doesn’t state whether notice is required.


Magic vs Wing: which is better?


It depends on what you’re comparing against. If you need a niche specialist role or the lowest published price for routine work, look at Wing’s general tier. If you want executive-level support, Magic’s Executive Assistant plan is about a dollar an hour more than Wing’s executive tier and includes backup coverage, more annual hours, and paid AI access.
